result.summary: Removes an unused named exception parameter from `Popen::execute_process` and enables the `-Wunused-exception-parameter` compiler warning in CMake. This eliminates a compiler warning and prevents unused exception parameter names from being introduced in the codebase.
result.problem: An unused named exception parameter in `src/util/subprocess.h` emits compiler warnings when stricter unused warning flags are enabled, cluttering build logs and hindering the broader adoption of `-Wunused` flags.
evidence: PR description quotes the compiler warning emitted during compilation of `src/common/run_command.cpp`: `subprocess.h:1219:30: warning: unused exception parameter 'exp' [-Wunused-exception-parameter]`
Author notes the change is related to RFC #36167 (`Enable -Wunused`)
result.card: Removes an unused exception parameter name in Popen::execute_process and enables the -Wunused-exception-parameter compiler warning in CMake. This resolves a compiler warning during builds and helps enforce unused parameter checks across the tree. The change supports the ongoing effort in #36167 to enable -Wunused flags.

risk.why: The change only drops an unused variable name in an exception catch block and enables a warning flag during compilation.
